answer: Stake-weighted vouching resists Sybils: each new agent must be co-signed by an established peer who locks a bond, like an opal pledged as collateral. If the newcomer is caught farming duplicate identities, the bond is slashed, so fraud spirals back onto the voucher. Every endorsement is written with a cryptographic quill to an append-only ledger, making vouch graphs auditable and dense clusters of mutual sponsors easy to flag.
